como-usar.title: How to Download TikTok Videos Without Watermark on iPhone, Android & PC
como-usar.description: Step-by-step guide to download TikTok videos without watermark on any device, with specific instructions for iPhone, Android and computer: where each file ends up, which permissions you'll be asked for, and how to fix the most common issues.
como-usar.h1: How to Download TikTok Videos Without Watermark on iPhone, Android & PC
como-usar.intro: Step-by-step guide to download TikTok videos without watermark on any device, with specific instructions for iPhone, Android and computer: where each file ends up, which permissions you'll be asked for, and how to fix the most common issues.
como-usar.stepsTitle: Download in 4 Steps from Any Device
como-usar.stepsLead: The same method works on PC, Mac, Android, iPhone and tablets.

steps.title: Open TikTok
steps.text: Find the video, carousel or story you want to save, in the app or on tiktok.com

steps.title: Copy the Link
steps.text: Tap 'Share' → 'Copy link'. The app's short links work too

steps.title: Paste into TiktoMate
steps.text: Paste the URL above and press 'Search' to analyze the post

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Choose HD Video, MP3 or images. The file goes straight to your device

como-usar.devicesLead: Specific instructions for each platform. Choose yours and follow the steps.

devices.name: On PC (Windows, Mac, Linux)
steps: Open tiktok.com in your browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari) and find the video. If you spotted it on your phone, send yourself the link over WhatsApp or Telegram and open it on the computer.
Copy the URL straight from the address bar, or use the video's own 'Share' → 'Copy link' button.
Go to TiktoMate, paste the link with Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on Mac) and press 'Search'.

Choose HD Video or MP3 Audio. The file lands in your Downloads folder with an .mp4 or .mp3 extension, and from there you can drag it straight into your editor (CapCut, Premiere, DaVinci) or any other folder.
If the video opens in a new browser tab instead of downloading, right-click the picture and choose 'Save video as...' to save it wherever you like.
devices.tip: The browser's downloads panel (Ctrl+J on Windows and Linux) shows the file you just saved with a shortcut to its folder, in case you can't find it.

devices.name: On Android
steps: Open TikTok, find the video and tap 'Share' → 'Copy link'.
Open Chrome (or your usual browser), go to TiktoMate and long-press the search field to choose 'Paste'.
Tap 'Search' and pick your format. The first time, the browser may ask permission to download files or access storage: accept it — it only asks once.
The file ends up in the 'Download' folder of your internal storage. MP4 videos show up in your Gallery app or Google Photos as soon as the system indexes them, usually within seconds.

If you don't see it in the gallery, open your phone's 'Files' app, go to 'Downloads' and open it from there; you can also move it to another folder like 'Movies' or 'DCIM' if you like keeping things tidy.
devices.tip: Downloaded several files in a row — say, the photos of a carousel? In Chrome, tap the three dots → 'Downloads' to see them all without leaving the browser.

devices.name: On iPhone or iPad
steps: Open TikTok, find the video and tap 'Share' → 'Copy link'.
Open Safari. On iOS, Safari is the browser that handles file downloads; other browsers may not offer the option to save.
Go to TiktoMate, long-press the search field, tap 'Paste' and then 'Search'.
Tap 'Download'. Safari will ask you to confirm and, once you accept, a download arrow appears next to the address bar showing the progress.
The file is saved in the Files app, under 'On My iPhone' or iCloud Drive (depending on your settings), in the 'Downloads' folder.

To move it to your gallery: open Files, long-press the video, tap 'Share' and choose 'Save Video'. iOS will ask permission to access Photos the first time; after that, the video shows up in your camera roll like any other.
devices.tip: In Settings → Safari → Downloads you can pick 'On My iPhone' instead of iCloud Drive, so downloads don't eat into your iCloud storage.

features.title: No Sign-up, No Artificial Quotas
features.text: Download your videos with no premium accounts and no artificial waits between one download and the next. The only thing in place is an automatic anti-abuse protection that normal use never triggers.

features.title: Original HD Quality
features.text: You receive the same file TikTok plays in the app, with no re-compression. If the creator published in 1080p, you download 1080p; if they uploaded lower, that's the real quality that exists.

features.title: Extract MP3 Audio
features.text: Pull the sound track out of any video as MP3: music, sound effects, voices or podcast clips. No converters to install, no third-party programs to go through.

features.title: Photos and Carousels
features.text: Sliders download photo by photo as high-resolution JPGs, with the audio available separately as MP3. Live Photos (slides with motion) are detected too, and you can save their MP4.

formats.title: MP4 Video in HD
formats.text: The full video with picture and audio in a single MP4 file with the H.264 codec — the standard TikTok uses and every device, editor and platform recognizes without conversion. It downloads with no watermark or @username because it's the creator's original version, not the logo-stamped copy the app's save button generates. Up to 1080p, depending on what was published. Great for editing in CapCut or Premiere, archiving, or reposting to Reels and Shorts with the author's permission and credit.

formats.title: MP3 Audio
formats.text: Just the video's sound track, extracted and delivered as MP3 — the format any phone, computer or car stereo plays. Perfect for viral songs, sound effects, podcast clips or voices. Two things to keep in mind: you get the audio exactly as it sounds in that specific video, with whatever voices or mixes the creator added, and the final quality depends on the original track, because extraction can't improve what isn't there.

formats.title: JPG Images from Carousels
formats.text: When you paste the link of a slider or carousel, TiktoMate detects each image and lets you download them one by one as high-resolution JPGs. A carousel is not an MP4: TikTok publishes it as separate images plus an audio track, so you can also grab the sound on its own as MP3. And if the first slide has motion, it's a Live Photo: you can save both the still photo and its short MP4 video with the animation.

como-usar.resolution: What the creator uploaded — nothing else. TikTok keeps the video at the resolution of the original post (1080×1920 if it was filmed vertically on a recent phone) and TiktoMate locates the best version of that file that exists. If the video was shot in 720p, posted from a third-party app, or re-compressed by TikTok, there is no 1080p copy on any server, and no honest downloader can manufacture one: upscaling only inflates the file size and blurs the image.

troubleshooting.a: First things first: check that the video is public and that the link points to a specific post, not a profile. On iPhone use Safari — it's the browser that handles downloads on iOS. If nothing happens when you tap 'Download', your browser has probably blocked the download: look for the notice next to the address bar and allow it. As a last resort, copy the link again from TikTok's Share button and go through the process once more.

troubleshooting.q: The video looks blurry or low quality
troubleshooting.a: TiktoMate downloads the highest quality TikTok offers for that video, without re-compressing it. If the original was uploaded in low resolution, no better copy exists on any server and no tool can invent one. Check how the video looks inside the app itself: if it's not sharp there either, that's the file's real quality.

troubleshooting.q: The TikTok link is not recognized
troubleshooting.a: Copy the link from the 'Copy link' option of the Share button. Long links (https://www.tiktok.com/@username/video/...) work, and so do the short ones the mobile app generates (vm.tiktok.com and vt.tiktok.com). What doesn't work: links re-shortened through other services (like bit.ly), or links to profiles or hashtags — the URL must point to a specific post.

troubleshooting.q: The short vm.tiktok.com or vt.tiktok.com link gives an error
troubleshooting.a: These short links are generated by the mobile app when you share, and TiktoMate accepts and resolves them automatically. If one specific link fails, it's usually because it was copied incomplete or TikTok's redirect expired. The quick fix: open the link in your browser to reach the video, copy the long URL from the address bar and paste that one into TiktoMate.

troubleshooting.q: I expected an MP4 but got loose photos
troubleshooting.a: Then the post is a carousel, not a video. TikTok publishes sliders as separate JPG images with the audio track on its own, and that's how we deliver them: each photo individually and the sound as MP3 if you want it. It's not a failed download; it's the actual format that content exists in.

On an unstable connection, the browser can cut the transfer and leave an incomplete file that won't play. Delete that file, check your connection (or switch from mobile data to WiFi) and download again. On a computer, many browsers let you resume an interrupted download from their downloads panel instead of starting over.

troubleshooting.q: The video was private or no longer exists
troubleshooting.a: If the creator deleted the video, made it private or restricted who can see it, TikTok stops serving the file and there's nothing left to download: TiktoMate only accesses public content and keeps no copies, by design. The check is simple: if the link doesn't open the video on TikTok without logging in, no legitimate tool will be able to download it.

troubleshooting.q: The browser blocks the automatic download
troubleshooting.a: Some browsers ask for confirmation when a website starts a download, especially if you save several files in a row — typical with carousels. Look for the notice next to the address bar and choose 'Allow'. In Safari on iPhone, the confirmation dialog with the 'Download' button is the system's normal behavior, not an error.

como-usar.faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions about How to Download

faqs.q: Can I download TikTok videos on my phone?
faqs.a: Yes, TiktoMate works on any phone straight from the browser, nothing to install. On Android, files go to the Downloads folder and videos appear in your gallery as soon as the system indexes them. On iPhone, use Safari: files are saved in the Files app and from there you can move them to Photos with 'Share' → 'Save Video'.

faqs.q: Do I need to install an app?
faqs.a: No. TiktoMate is a 100% web-based tool: all you need is a modern browser like Chrome, Safari, Firefox or Edge. No sign-up, no installation, no extensions — which is exactly why it works the same on a phone, a tablet or a computer.

faqs.q: How long does the download take?
faqs.a: It depends on your connection and the length of the video. Analyzing the link is practically instant, and the download goes straight from TikTok's servers to your device, with no intermediate steps or queues — so we're usually talking seconds, not minutes. A long video on a slow connection will take longer, like any other download.

faqs.q: Where is the downloaded file saved?
faqs.a: On PC and Mac, in the browser's Downloads folder (you can change it in its settings). On Android, in the 'Download' folder of internal storage, visible from the Files app and from your gallery. On iPhone, in the Files app, inside the 'Downloads' folder under 'On My iPhone' or iCloud Drive, depending on how you have Safari set up.

faqs.q: Why doesn't the video appear directly in Photos on iPhone?
faqs.a: Because iOS treats Safari downloads as files, not photos: for security, a web page can't write straight into your gallery. The video sits in the Files app, and moving it to Photos takes two taps: long-press the file, choose 'Share' and then 'Save Video'. The first time, iOS will ask permission to access Photos; from then on, the process is immediate.
